# Moreland Associates

Your resource for seasoned interim executive leaders who specialize in leading companies to market traction.

How we help

## Interim executive leadership

Every company’s road to market traction runs through a series of milestones. When the next one calls for a different leader than the one you have, or one you don’t have yet, we step in. Moreland’s interim executives lead from the inside: setting the strategy, executing it, and building the team and systems that keep delivering long after we’re gone.

### [Interim CMO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/#roles)

Own the market with an AI-first go-to-market: positioning, messaging, awareness and the engine that turns it into pipeline, built for how buyers now find and evaluate you, including AI search and chat assistants. Connect what the market is telling you to the product team, and what you build to customers and investors.

### [Interim COO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/#roles)

Turn a promising company into a well-run one with an AI-first operating model: the cadence, processes, tools and team to scale without breaking what already works.

### [Interim CCO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/#roles)

Lead the whole commercial engine, from marketing through sales, onboarding and customer success, with AI-first commercial operations, so early wins become repeatable revenue.

### Why interim, not fractional

Roles like CMO, COO and CCO sit at the center of the business: information flows in from the market, out from product and engineering, and up to the board and investors. Part-time leadership in these seats slows everyone down. Fractional works well for finance or IT. For the roles that run the business, you need someone in the seat.

### When to bring in an interim executive

- You’re pivoting or reaching a milestone, and the leader you need next is different from the one you have.
- You’ve chosen your beachhead segment and need someone to lead now and help you hire the right permanent person.
- Your go-to-market needs rebuilding, AI-first, for how buyers now discover and evaluate vendors.
- You’re not sure yet what the role should look like.
- You need help now, not after a six-month search.

[More about interim executive services](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/)

## Market Traction

Market traction is having a dominant position in a market segment. It’s also called a beachhead. Driving to this point requires passion, agility, focus, commitment, and vision. In a word, entrepreneurship.

1. [Eureka](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/eureka/): Stage one of market traction: your product is working and ready for customers. Next comes first revenue.
2. [Kaa Ching](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/kaa-ching/): Stage two of market traction: first revenue. Next comes building reference accounts your target buyers recognize.
3. [Two Thumbs Up](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/two-thumbs-up/): Stage three of market traction: credible reference accounts. Next comes choosing a beachhead segment and building momentum.
4. [Momentum](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/momentum/): Stage four of market traction: the whole company is focused on one segment with a predictable pipeline. Next comes building buzz.
5. [Building Buzz](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/building-buzz/): Stage five of market traction: you are a recognized key player in your target segment. Next comes segment dominance.
6. [Market Traction](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/market-traction/): Stage six: market traction. Your company dominates its segment and can afford to expand into the next one.

_The Milestones to Market Traction. Select a milestone to learn more, or [take the test](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/test/) to find yours._

Services

# Interim Executive

Bring in the seasoned C-level, marketing, commercial, and operations executive talent you need on an interim basis.

## About interim executive services

Sourcing the right talent for your team is vital to your company’s success. Hiring the wrong leader can be both an expensive and disruptive mistake. Moreland’s interim executive service provides you a seasoned executive immediately.

## Interim roles

Our seasoned executives have 20+ years of experience and step into these interim roles:

- **Interim Chief Marketing Officer (CMO):** own the market with an AI-first go-to-market: positioning, messaging, awareness and the engine that turns it into pipeline, built for how buyers now find and evaluate you, including AI search and chat assistants. Connect what the market is telling you to the product team, and what you build to customers and investors.
- **Interim Chief Operating Officer (COO):** turn a promising company into a well-run one with an AI-first operating model: the cadence, processes, tools and team to scale without breaking what already works.
- **Interim Chief Commercial Officer (CCO):** lead the whole commercial engine, from marketing through sales, onboarding and customer success, with AI-first commercial operations, so early wins become repeatable revenue.

If necessary, we can field an entire team.

## Why interim, not fractional

Roles like CMO, COO and CCO sit at the center of the business: information flows in from the market, out from product and engineering, and up to the board and investors. Part-time leadership in these seats slows everyone down. Fractional works well for finance or IT. For the roles that run the business, you need someone in the seat.

Our interim executives have experience in everything from venture-funded technology start-ups to large enterprises. Our forte is parachuting into an assignment, seamlessly becoming a member of the team and making an immediate impact on the needs of the company.

As entrepreneurs, we think first about the business and what it needs to achieve to hit the next milestone. Our recommendations and actions are always in support of achieving the company’s success and building [market traction](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/).

We’re biased to action and believe in quickly getting the game in play; working hand-in-hand with sales; spending shrewdly to produce results; and providing transparency, metrics and persistent value.

We work closely with the executive team to identify the ideal permanent candidate for the position and to ensure a seamless transition once the person is hired.

## When to use an interim CxO

Companies elect to use an interim executive in situations like these:

- The company closed funding and has imminent go-to-market needs, but lacks a key executive on the team.
- The company wants to make sure it hires the right person – not the first qualified person it interviews.
- The company has parted ways with an executive.
- The company has pivoted to a new market segment or business model and needs the right person to build traction in the new segment.
- The company wants or needs to enter a new market and doesn’t want to distract the existing leadership from executing in current markets.
- The company’s go-to-market needs rebuilding, AI-first, for how buyers now discover and evaluate vendors.

When big market shifts occur, such as a global economic downturn or the implosion of a market sector, the need to find a new successful market is imperative. An interim executive is a great option for quickly bringing in the seasoned management talent you need until you are ready to add to your permanent staff.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an interim executive?

A senior leader who steps into a role such as CMO, COO or CCO for a defined period, leading the function from the inside, usually through a specific milestone such as a pivot, a funding round or choosing a beachhead segment.

### What's the difference between an interim and a fractional executive?

An interim executive works in the role full time; a fractional executive splits time across several companies. Fractional works well for finance or IT. Cross-functional roles like CMO, COO and CCO sit at the center of the business, and part-time leadership in those seats slows everyone down.

### Which interim roles does Moreland provide?

Interim Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), Chief Operating Officer (COO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO), each with an AI-first approach. If needed, we can field a whole team.

### When should a company bring in an interim executive?

When the next milestone calls for a leader you don't have: after a pivot or a funding round, when an executive departs, once you've chosen a beachhead segment, when go-to-market needs rebuilding for how buyers now find vendors, or when you're not yet sure what the role should look like.

### How long does an interim engagement last?

Typically several months, often four to nine, depending on the milestone. Many engagements end once the company has hired the right permanent leader, with our help.

### Can an interim executive help hire the permanent leader?

Yes. We work closely with the executive team to identify the ideal permanent candidate and to ensure a seamless handover once they're hired.

### What does “AI-first go-to-market” mean?

Going to market the way buyers now find and evaluate vendors: being visible in AI search and chat assistants, and running marketing and commercial operations on AI tools from day one rather than adding them later.

# About Moreland Associates

Interim executive leaders who take technology companies to their next milestone, and leave them stronger than they found them.

## Who we are

Moreland Associates is a select group of senior executives with proven abilities in entrepreneurship, leadership, strategy and execution. Our experience ranges from leading functions in mature companies to founding technology start-ups. CEOs, boards and venture capital partners bring us in when the next milestone calls for leadership they don’t yet have.

We aren’t a bench of resumes. We’re executives who have worked together, operate under one banner and one philosophy, and know each other’s strengths well. When a company needs more than one leader, we can field a team that already works as one.

## How we work

- **The business comes first.** We start with what your business needs right now, whether that’s revenue, the team, the go-to-market engine or the operating model, and we stay only as long as our work keeps serving that need.
- **Strategy and execution, together.** Strategy is useless without execution, and execution without strategy is inefficient and likely to fail. We set the direction and then do the work.
- **Persistent value.** The value we create should last long after we’re gone. That means building the systems, processes and teams that keep delivering, not just doing the job while we’re there.
- **Experience, not playbooks.** Every company is different, especially in the start-up world. We bring pattern recognition from decades of doing this work, not a cookie-cutter method.

title: "What Is Market Traction?"

Market Traction

# About market traction

Emerging markets offer a precious opportunity to produce huge investment returns.

Once a start-up can establish a dominant position in a market, it’s tough to dislodge – even for larger, more established players. That’s why building market traction is critical. Without it, failure is almost always the result for start-ups.

A company has achieved market traction when its product is being predictably sold to buyers in the same market segment.

The company knows the sales cycle and has established a pipeline of orders. This market segment then serves as the beachhead from which all subsequent market share will be won.

There are six main milestones on the road to market traction.

## The Milestones to Market Traction

1. [Eureka](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/eureka/): Stage one of market traction: your product is working and ready for customers. Next comes first revenue.
2. [Kaa Ching](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/kaa-ching/): Stage two of market traction: first revenue. Next comes building reference accounts your target buyers recognize.
3. [Two Thumbs Up](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/two-thumbs-up/): Stage three of market traction: credible reference accounts. Next comes choosing a beachhead segment and building momentum.
4. [Momentum](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/momentum/): Stage four of market traction: the whole company is focused on one segment with a predictable pipeline. Next comes building buzz.
5. [Building Buzz](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/building-buzz/): Stage five of market traction: you are a recognized key player in your target segment. Next comes segment dominance.
6. [Market Traction](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/market-traction/): Stage six: market traction. Your company dominates its segment and can afford to expand into the next one.

_This model describes the evolution of a technology company from inception through the achievement of market traction. Select a milestone for an explanation of each._

Each milestone has unique requirements for marketing and sales. When in alignment, marketing and sales work in concert as a powerful market traction engine.

A young company’s resources and time are limited, and can all too easily evaporate in the absence of an effective plan. An effective plan exploits the company’s early entry position and maximizes return on investment.

[Explore the six stages](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/) or [take the test](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/test/) to find out where your company is today.

## Momentum: choosing your beachhead

Momentum is the inflection point on the curve. It’s where you choose the market segment in which you’ll build your beachhead, and it’s the trickiest milestone on the road to market traction.

A beachhead is a defensible, dominant position in one segment. That doesn’t mean owning 51% of the market. It means being bigger than anyone else in that segment.

### Differentiation comes first

The segment you choose should be one where your competitive differentiation is tied to what makes you different from everyone else. You don’t want to spend your resources defending against a legitimate competitor; you want to be unlike any other option. That makes differentiation the number one criterion for every candidate segment.

### The ideal path

1. Hypothesize the segments you could win.
2. Test the first one by trying to achieve repeat sales.
3. When you get repeat sales, move on to the second segment.
4. Once you have at least two, and ideally three or four, choose the segment in which to build your beachhead.

By then you know everything you need to know about selling into each segment: how long it takes to sell, who to sell to, what you can charge, how you beat the competition and why your value proposition is essential. That isn’t the usual path, but it’s the one that takes the most risk out of the decision.

### Why investors care

Investors are looking for risk reduction. Ideas are plentiful, and technical execution is rarely what holds a company back. The ability to find and serve a market is still a real differentiator, and a company that has tested its segments this way can show it.

### A common moment for an interim executive

The leader who gets you to your beachhead isn’t always the one who builds on it. Once the segment is chosen, you may need someone with deep domain knowledge or a reputation in that market. An [interim executive](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/) can lead you through the choice and then help you bring in the right permanent leader.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is market traction?

A company has market traction when its product is being predictably sold to buyers in the same market segment. It knows the sales cycle, has a pipeline of orders, and holds a dominant position in that segment, called a beachhead.

### What is a beachhead market?

A defensible, dominant position in one market segment. It doesn't mean owning a majority of the market; it means being bigger than anyone else in that segment. It's the base from which all later market share is won.

### What are the Milestones to Market Traction?

Six stages a technology company passes through: Eureka (a working product), Kaa Ching (first revenue), Two Thumbs Up (credible reference customers), Momentum (choosing the beachhead segment), Building Buzz (becoming a recognized key player) and Market Traction (dominating the segment).

### How do you choose a beachhead segment?

Make competitive differentiation the first criterion. Hypothesize candidate segments, test the first by trying to achieve repeat sales, then the next. Once at least two (ideally three or four) have been tested, choose the one in which to build your beachhead.

### What is the Market Traction Test?

Six yes-or-no questions that take about 30 seconds and show which milestone your company has reached, the milestones you've passed and those that lie ahead.

## Accelerating market traction

Moreland Associates specializes in helping companies accelerate market traction. If your company is ready to get to market traction faster and with fewer resources, we’re ready to work with you.

---
title: "The Six Stages of Market Traction"
url: https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/
description: "The six milestones a technology company passes on the road to market traction: Eureka, Kaa Ching, Two Thumbs Up, Momentum, Building Buzz and Market Traction."
---

Market Traction

# The six stages of market traction

From a working product to segment dominance, there are predictable milestones on the way. Each has its own marketing and sales requirements.

1. [Eureka](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/eureka/): Stage one of market traction: your product is working and ready for customers. Next comes first revenue.
2. [Kaa Ching](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/kaa-ching/): Stage two of market traction: first revenue. Next comes building reference accounts your target buyers recognize.
3. [Two Thumbs Up](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/two-thumbs-up/): Stage three of market traction: credible reference accounts. Next comes choosing a beachhead segment and building momentum.
4. [Momentum](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/momentum/): Stage four of market traction: the whole company is focused on one segment with a predictable pipeline. Next comes building buzz.
5. [Building Buzz](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/building-buzz/): Stage five of market traction: you are a recognized key player in your target segment. Next comes segment dominance.
6. [Market Traction](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/market-traction/): Stage six: market traction. Your company dominates its segment and can afford to expand into the next one.

Stage one of six

## [Eureka](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/eureka/)

### It’s exciting to see your idea manifested in a working product!

From the beginning, you’ve envisioned the finished product and how it would work. Now it’s really here and ready for the customers.

### What’s next?

Focus will now shift to making the first sales and preparing to ship, install, invoice, and receive payment. In other words, to make your cash register ring — Kaa Ching!

Stage two of six

## [Kaa Ching](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/kaa-ching/)

### First revenue — that’s great!

To get that first revenue is such a satisfying feeling. Sure, it’s probably from another small local company that you have ties with, but it’s money in the bank.

### What’s next?

The next challenge is to develop reference accounts that are recognizable to the companies you are targeting. Reference companies have the key problem your product is designed to address and will serve as credible references to other buyers. This phase is called Two Thumbs Up.

Stage three of six

## [Two Thumbs Up](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/two-thumbs-up/)

### You closed some key accounts — amazing!

The fact that these companies have purchased and are happy tells prospects that your product works and you can deliver.

### What’s next?

Now, you’ve got to leverage this credibility to build momentum. You must evaluate the various market segments you are currently selling into, select the one in which you will build a beachhead, and then focus the company on this segment.

Stage four of six

## [Momentum](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/momentum/)

### The entire company is focused on dominating the selected market segment.

You have a sales pipeline and are getting better at identifying, selling, and closing sales with the target buyers.

### What’s next?

The next challenge is to build a broader awareness, and elevate your visibility so that the sale begins before your reps contact the target buyer.

[Read more: how to choose your beachhead segment](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/#momentum)

Stage five of six

## [Building Buzz](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/building-buzz/)

### Congrats — you’re a key player in your target segment!

This means your sales cycle should be shortening, since the target buyer knows who you are before your sales rep contacts them. It’s also known that your product is worthy of consideration by a target buyer — even before they are ready to buy. Your next challenge is to dominate the segment and reach the Market Traction milestone.

Stage six of six

## [Market Traction](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/market-traction/)

### You’ve done it!

Your company has dominated the selected market segment. Prospective buyers in this segment automatically look to your company for a solution. The stamp of credibility of the press and analysts helped fill your sales pipeline and made you attractive to strategic partners. Now, your company is in the driver’s seat for this segment and you can afford to go after a new segment and expand. Contact us to learn how Moreland can help you capitalize on your success.

[Find your stage: take the test](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/test/) · [Talk with us](https://www.morelandassoc.com/get-started/?topic=market-traction)

## Ready to build market traction?

Talk with a Moreland executive about where your company is today and what it will take to reach the next milestone.

---
title: "Interim CMO vs Fractional CMO: Which Do You Need?"
url: https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/interim-vs-fractional-cmo/
description: "An interim CMO leads marketing full time through a milestone; a fractional CMO works part time across several companies. How to choose, and when each fits."
---

Insights

# Interim CMO vs fractional CMO: which does your company need?

An interim CMO leads your marketing full time through a specific milestone. A fractional CMO works part time, splitting the week across several companies. Leading marketing is cross-functional and time-sensitive. Consistent availability, smooth responsive operations, and coordinated work need full-time executive leadership.

Updated October 2026

## The difference at a glance

Interim CMOFractional CMO TimeFull time, in your companyPart time, often one or two days a week FocusYour company onlyShared across several clients LengthSet by a milestone, often four to nine monthsOpen-ended retainer Role on the leadership teamA full member: in the meetings, owning the numbersAn advisor who drops in Best forLeading change: a launch, a pivot, a new segment, rebuilding go-to-marketSteady oversight of a plan that already works The permanent CMODefines the role and helps you hireUsually not involved

## Why the CMO seat is hard to fill part time

The CMO sits at the center of the business. Information flows in from the market, out from product and engineering, and up to the board and investors. Sales needs answers this week, not next Tuesday. When the person connecting all of that is only there part of the time, everyone else waits, and the company slows down.

That's why we believe in interim, not fractional, for the roles that run the business. Fractional works well for functions with clear boundaries and a steady rhythm, such as finance or IT. Marketing at a growing technology company is rarely either.

## When a fractional CMO makes sense

Fractional is a good fit when the need is narrow and steady:

- An early company needs senior marketing judgement, but not yet a leader in the seat.
- The plan is working and the team is solid; it needs periodic oversight, not change.
- Budget only allows part-time help, and the stakes of moving slowly are low.

## Signs you need an interim CMO

- You’ve closed funding and have go-to-market goals, but no marketing leader.
- Your CMO has left, and the pipeline can’t wait for a six-month search.
- You’ve pivoted, or chosen a new [beachhead segment](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/#momentum), and positioning, messaging and the team all need to change.
- Your go-to-market needs rebuilding for how buyers now find vendors, including [AI search and chat assistants](https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/ai-first-go-to-market/).
- You aren’t sure yet what the permanent CMO role should look like.

## How we work as interim CMOs

Moreland’s interim CMOs step in full time, set the strategy, execute it, and build the team and systems that keep delivering after we leave. We work closely with you to define the permanent role and hire the right person, then hand over cleanly. Read more about [interim executive services](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/), or see [how long an engagement usually lasts](https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/how-long-interim-executive-engagement/).

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the difference between an interim CMO and a fractional CMO?

An interim CMO works in your company full time for a defined period, usually through a specific milestone. A fractional CMO works part time, often a day or two a week, and splits their time across several companies.

### Is an interim CMO more expensive than a fractional CMO?

Per month, yes, because it's a full-time role. The better comparison is against what's at stake: a delayed launch, a missed segment or a stalled pipeline usually costs far more than the difference.

### When does a fractional CMO make sense?

When the need is narrow and steady: an early company that needs senior marketing advice but not a leader in the seat, or a team with a solid plan that needs periodic oversight.

### Does an interim CMO help hire the permanent CMO?

Yes. Defining the role and helping hire the right permanent leader is part of the job, followed by a clean handover.

[Talk with us about an interim CMO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/get-started/?topic=interim-executive)

---
title: "How Long Does an Interim Executive Engagement Last?"
url: https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/how-long-interim-executive-engagement/
description: "Interim executive engagements typically last four to nine months. The milestone sets the length: most end once it is reached and a permanent leader is hired."
---

Insights

# How long does an interim executive engagement last?

Typically four to nine months. The length is set by the milestone, not the calendar: most engagements end once the company has reached it and hired the right permanent leader.

Updated October 2026

## What sets the length

- **The milestone.** Launching into a new segment, rebuilding go-to-market or getting operations ready to scale each take a different amount of time. We agree on the milestone at the start.
- **The permanent hire.** If the engagement includes defining the role and hiring the permanent leader, the search and handover add time.
- **The size of the gap.** Stepping into a working team is quicker than building one, or replacing processes that no longer fit.
- **Outside timelines.** A board meeting, a funding round or a product launch can set a natural end point.

## What a typical engagement looks like

Every engagement is different, but most follow a similar shape:

1. **The first month: assess and act.** Learn the business, the market and the team quickly. Fix what’s urgent, and agree on the plan and how progress will be measured.
2. **The middle months: execute and build.** Run the plan. Build the team, processes and systems that will keep delivering, AI-first from the start.
3. **The final phase: hire and hand over.** Define the permanent role, help hire the right person, and hand over a working function with the plan, metrics and team in place.

## Shorter and longer engagements

A focused project, such as repositioning before a funding round, can take less time. A pivot, an entry into a new market or a company that needs a whole leadership function built from scratch can take longer. If the milestone moves, the engagement can move with it.

## Planning for a good ending

The best engagements are designed to end well. Define the milestone up front. Start thinking about the permanent role early, because the interim executive is often the best person to shape it. And plan an overlap, so the new leader inherits a working function rather than a to-do list.

Not sure whether you need interim or fractional help? Read [interim CMO vs fractional CMO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/interim-vs-fractional-cmo/), or see [how our interim executives work](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/).

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does an interim executive engagement last?

Typically four to nine months. The length depends on the milestone the company needs to reach, and most engagements end once it's reached and the right permanent leader has been hired.

### Can an interim engagement be extended?

Yes. If the milestone moves, for example after a pivot or a new funding round, the engagement can be extended. We agree up front how to review progress and adjust.

### How quickly can an interim executive start?

Much faster than a permanent hire, which often takes several months to search, interview and negotiate. Tell us your timeline and we'll tell you what's possible.

### What happens at the end of an interim engagement?

A planned handover. The interim executive helps hire the permanent leader, overlaps with them where possible, and leaves the plan, team, processes and metrics in place.

[Talk with us about your timeline](https://www.morelandassoc.com/get-started/?topic=interim-executive)

---
title: "When Should a Start-up Hire an Interim COO?"
url: https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/when-to-hire-interim-coo/
description: "Hire an interim COO when growth, funding or a pivot creates more operating work than founders can carry. The signs, the role, and why interim first."
---

Insights

# When should a start-up hire an interim COO?

When the company has outgrown the way it runs. Growth, funding or a pivot has created more operating work than the founders can carry, and you need it fixed now, while you work out what the permanent role should be.

Updated October 2026

## Signs it’s time

- **The founders are the bottleneck.** Decisions queue up behind the CEO, who is also selling, fundraising and managing the product.
- **You’ve just raised money.** The plan in the pitch deck now has to happen, with more people, more spending and more scrutiny from the board.
- **What used to work is breaking.** Processes that worked for 15 people don’t work for 50: handoffs drop, priorities collide and nobody is sure who owns what.
- **There’s no operating rhythm.** No consistent planning, metrics or meeting cadence, so problems surface late.
- **An executive has left,** or the company is preparing for an acquisition, a new market or rapid scale.

## What an interim COO does

An interim COO turns a promising company into a well-run one:

- Sets the operating cadence: planning, goals, metrics and the meetings that keep everyone aligned.
- Fixes or builds the processes and tools the company needs to scale, without breaking what already works.
- Puts an AI-first operating model in place, using AI tools in day-to-day operations from the start rather than adding them later.
- Strengthens the team, including hiring for the gaps.
- Frees the CEO to focus on customers, product, investors and the vision.

## Why interim first

No C-suite role varies more than the COO. In one company it means running operations and finance; in another it means owning go-to-market or product delivery. It usually fills whatever the CEO doesn’t do. That makes the permanent COO one of the hardest hires to get right.

An interim COO solves the immediate problem and shows you what the role actually needs to be. When you hire the permanent COO, you’re hiring for a defined job, with someone who has done it in your company helping you choose.

Part-time help rarely works here. The COO sits at the center of the business, and operations problems don’t wait for a fractional executive’s next day in the office.

## COO or CCO?

If the problem is mostly about revenue — marketing, sales and customer success pulling in different directions — you may need a commercial leader rather than an operational one. See [what a Chief Commercial Officer does](https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/what-does-a-cco-do/).

Read more about our [interim COO, CMO and CCO roles](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/), or [how long an engagement usually lasts](https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/how-long-interim-executive-engagement/).

## Frequently asked questions

### When should a start-up hire an interim COO?

When growth, funding or a pivot has created more operating work than the founders can carry, things that used to work are starting to break, and you need it fixed now while you work out what the permanent COO role should be.

### What does an interim COO do?

Sets the operating cadence, planning and metrics; fixes or builds the processes, tools and team the company needs to scale; puts an AI-first operating model in place; and helps define and hire the permanent COO.

### Why hire an interim COO instead of a permanent one?

The COO role varies more than any other C-suite role, because it fills whatever the CEO doesn't do. An interim COO lets you find out what your company actually needs before you hire for it.

### What's the difference between a COO and a CCO?

A COO runs how the company operates: planning, processes, people and systems across the business. A CCO runs how the company makes money: marketing, sales, onboarding and customer success as one commercial engine.

[Talk with us about an interim COO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/get-started/?topic=interim-executive)

---
title: "What Does a Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) Do?"
url: https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/what-does-a-cco-do/
description: "A Chief Commercial Officer runs marketing, sales, onboarding and customer success as one revenue engine. How it differs from a CMO or CRO, and when you need one."
---

Insights

# What does a Chief Commercial Officer do, and when do you need one?

A Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) owns the whole revenue engine — marketing, sales, onboarding and customer success — and runs it as one system. You need one when those functions are pulling in different directions and early wins aren’t turning into repeatable revenue.

Updated October 2026

## What a CCO is responsible for

- **One commercial plan:** which segments to win, with what offer, at what price, through which channels.
- **The full customer path:** from first awareness through the sale, onboarding, adoption, renewal and expansion.
- **The handoffs:** marketing to sales, sales to onboarding, onboarding to customer success, where deals and customers most often get lost.
- **Shared goals and data:** one view of pipeline, revenue and retention that every commercial team works from.
- **Commercial operations:** the processes, tools and AI-first systems that make the engine predictable.

## CCO, CMO, CRO and head of sales

RoleUsually owns Chief Commercial OfficerThe whole commercial engine: marketing, sales, onboarding and customer success Chief Marketing OfficerThe market: positioning, messaging, awareness and pipeline Chief Revenue OfficerRevenue targets, usually centered on the sales organization Head of salesThe sales team, deals and forecast

Titles vary from company to company. What matters is whether someone owns the revenue engine end to end.

## Signs you need a CCO

- Marketing and sales disagree about lead quality, and nobody can settle it with data.
- Deals stall or customers churn at the handoffs between teams.
- You’ve reached [Two Thumbs Up](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/two-thumbs-up/) or [Momentum](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/stages/momentum/), and now need repeatable revenue in one segment rather than heroic one-off wins.
- The CEO is still the de facto head of the commercial team.
- You’re entering a new segment or market and need the whole commercial approach to change at once.

## Why an interim CCO

Bringing the commercial functions together is a change project as much as a leadership role. An interim CCO can do the hard part — aligning the teams, the plan, the data and the handoffs — then help you decide whether you need a permanent CCO, or a strong CMO and head of sales working from one plan.

Read more about our [interim CCO, CMO and COO roles](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/), or compare with [when to hire an interim COO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/when-to-hire-interim-coo/).

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a Chief Commercial Officer do?

A CCO owns the whole commercial engine, from marketing through sales, onboarding and customer success, and runs it as one system with shared goals, data and handoffs, so early wins become repeatable revenue.

### What's the difference between a CCO and a CMO?

A CMO owns the market: positioning, messaging, awareness and the pipeline it creates. A CCO owns the full revenue path, including marketing, sales and customer success. In many companies the CMO reports to the CCO.

### What's the difference between a CCO and a CRO?

The titles overlap and companies use them differently. A CRO is usually focused on revenue targets and the sales organization; a CCO typically has a broader remit across the whole commercial engine, including how the company goes to market and keeps customers.

### When does a company need a CCO?

When marketing, sales and customer success are pulling in different directions, handoffs between them are losing deals or customers, and early wins aren't turning into predictable revenue.

[Talk with us about an interim CCO](https://www.morelandassoc.com/get-started/?topic=interim-executive)

---

Moreland Associates · (510) 833-7308 · info@morelandassoc.com · 2532 Santa Clara Avenue, Suite 413, Alameda, CA 94501 · https://www.morelandassoc.com/


---
title: "What Is an AI-First Go-to-Market?"
url: https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/ai-first-go-to-market/
description: "An AI-first go-to-market reaches buyers where they now find vendors, including AI assistants, and runs marketing and sales on AI from day one."
---

Insights

# What is an AI-first go-to-market?

Going to market the way buyers now find and evaluate vendors. That means being visible, and accurately described, in AI search and chat assistants as well as traditional search, and running marketing and commercial operations on AI tools from the start rather than bolting them on later.

Updated October 2026

## Why it matters now

Business buyers increasingly start their research by asking an AI assistant, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot or Google’s AI answers, before they visit a vendor’s website or talk to sales. The assistant summarizes the options and often names a shortlist. If your company isn’t in that answer, or is described inaccurately, you may never get the call.

At the same time, AI tools have changed what a small marketing and sales team can do: research, content, personalization and pipeline management that once needed a much larger team.

## What changes in practice

1. **Being found in AI answers.** Clear, specific content that answers the questions your buyers ask; the same description of your company everywhere; credible mentions on other sites; and a website built for AI tools to read, with structured data and clean pages.
2. **Content built around questions.** Pages that give a direct answer first, then the detail, rather than marketing copy that makes the reader dig.
3. **AI in commercial operations from day one.** Research, account planning, content production, personalization, pipeline management and forecasting, with people making the judgement calls.
4. **A team built for it.** Fewer handoffs, new skills, and clear rules for how AI is used and checked.

## What doesn’t change

The fundamentals of [market traction](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/) still apply. You still need to choose a [beachhead segment](https://www.morelandassoc.com/market-traction/#momentum), be distinctly different in it, and build credible reference customers. AI amplifies a clear position and exposes a fuzzy one: if you can’t say crisply who you’re for and why you’re different, an AI assistant can’t either.

## Where to start

- Ask the AI assistants your buyers use how they describe your company and your category. Note what’s missing or wrong.
- Write down the 10 questions your buyers ask most, and make sure your website answers each one directly.
- Make your company description consistent across your website, LinkedIn, Google Business Profile and directories.
- Pick one commercial process, such as account research or proposal writing, and rebuild it with AI tools.

## How we help

Moreland’s interim CMOs and CCOs build AI-first go-to-market and commercial operations as part of the job, not as a separate project. Read more about our [interim executive roles](https://www.morelandassoc.com/services/interim-executive/), or see [why the CMO seat needs someone full time](https://www.morelandassoc.com/insights/interim-vs-fractional-cmo/).

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an AI-first go-to-market?

Going to market the way buyers now find and evaluate vendors: being visible and accurately described in AI search and chat assistants as well as traditional search, and running marketing and commercial operations on AI tools from the start rather than adding them later.

### Is AI-first go-to-market just using AI tools in marketing?

No. Tools are part of it, but the bigger change is on the buyer's side. Buyers increasingly research and shortlist vendors with AI assistants, so your positioning has to be clear and consistent enough for those assistants to describe you accurately.

### How do you get a company recommended by AI assistants?

Publish clear, specific answers to the questions your buyers ask; describe your company the same way everywhere; earn credible mentions on other sites; and make your website easy for AI tools to read, with structured data and clean, crawlable pages.

### Does AI-first go-to-market replace positioning and segment focus?

No. AI amplifies a clear position and exposes a fuzzy one. Choosing your beachhead segment and being distinctly different in it matter more, not less.

[Talk with us about your go-to-market](https://www.morelandassoc.com/get-started/?topic=interim-executive)

Market Traction

# Market Traction Test

Where is your company on the road to market traction?

## About the Traction Test

From concept phase, through product development and segment dominance, there are predictable milestones a technology start-up will pass on the way. We specialize in helping technology companies address the sales and marketing challenges at each phase and accelerate the time to market traction.

## Take the test

Take 30 seconds to fill out the test below and pinpoint your current position on the road to market traction. Once you’re done, we’ll show you the milestones you’ve passed and those that lie ahead.

1. Is the product developed and ready for sale to a customer for a “live” deployment?
2. Have you sold, shipped, installed, invoiced, and been paid for your first product?
3. Do you have customers who are credible to your prospects?
4. Have you targeted a single market segment, and are your salespeople increasingly able to predict their closure rate for prospects in that segment?
5. Do the industry analysts recognize your company as having the #1, #2, or #3 product in the market segment?
6. Are you the dominant player in the target segment?
